subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose ordinary plugin runtime access to plugin-registered Gateway methods, and should that surface be raw dispatch, an allowlisted request API, or typed service/capability contracts?
rationale: The API shape changes the public Plugin SDK and the Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract or security policy.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, authorization rules, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep only the route-scoped helper
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls and document authenticated HTTP-route dispatch as the supported boundary.

options.title: Expose raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Add a generic method-string caller and explicitly accept the larger security and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, authorization rules, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest history match for the existing route-scoped dispatch contract and adjacent Gateway/Plugin SDK boundary.
